title: LLM Training Pipeline, Tool Use & Fine-Tuning
session_goals: Build foundations for understanding how LLMs are trained
Demystify pre-training, post-training (SFT), and model serving
Introduce tool calling / function calls as a fine-tuning outcome
Survey preference optimization algorithms (GRPO, DPO, PPO)
agenda: Pre-training (how a base model is built)

concepts.name: Pre-training
concepts.definition: First stage of LLM training. Public datasets (e.g., FineWeb2, BigCode, SWE-rebench, NASA, Google's private corpora) are passed through a transformer. The model learns language structure, grammar, world knowledge — 'most of the intelligence' is here.

concepts.name: Base Model
concepts.definition: The output of pre-training. Knows how to construct English sentences; has world knowledge in weights. Not yet format/tone-aligned.

concepts.name: Pre-training Data Pipeline
concepts.definition: clone sources → filter (e.g., license, file-type) → near-deduplicate → tokenize. Example: BigCode: 220M GitHub repos → 102 TB → 30% file filter → 6.4 TB after license+dedupe → 3 TB final.

concepts.name: Fill-in-the-Blank Training
concepts.definition: Each sentence of N tokens is converted into N training questions, one per token. Sentence 'There is no tomorrow.' → 'There is no ___' at each position. Predicts the next token at every position simultaneously.
concepts.efficiency: N tokens = N training signals per sentence

concepts.name: Masking Recap
concepts.definition: Same as Recording 51 — prevents looking ahead. Crucial for turning 1 sentence into N training pairs.

concepts.name: Training Loop
concepts.definition: Predict token → compare to expected → compute loss (cross-entropy) → backprop → update weights. All weights inside transformer (Q/K/V matrices, feed-forward, embedding, linear layer) are updated.

concepts.name: Cross-Entropy Loss
concepts.definition: Loss = -log(p_expected_token) + sum(-log(1 - p_other_tokens)). If p_expected = 1, loss = 0. If model assigns wrong token high probability, loss → ∞.
concepts.intuition: Right prediction = 0. Wrong prediction = blow up.

concepts.name: Sigmoid (conceptual)
concepts.definition: Used in the class as a teaching tool for understanding loss. Sigmoid of 20 ≈ 1, sigmoid of -20 ≈ 0. Modern RLHF/preference optimization uses other functions (GRPO, DPO, PPO), but sigmoid is the conceptual anchor.
concepts.note: In production: GRPO (DeepSeek, popular for math/code), DPO, PPO are used.

concepts.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
concepts.definition: Second stage. Take use-case-specific data (e.g., sales calls, transcripts) and fine-tune the model. Changes tone, format, jargon. 'Most of the behavior is here.'

concepts.name: Post-Training
concepts.definition: Umbrella term for SFT and preference optimization. Where the model acquires the right format, tone, and tool-use behavior.

concepts.name: Preference Optimization (RLHF family)
concepts.definition: Algorithms that learn from preference data (which output is better) instead of just human-written outputs. Variants: GRPO, DPO, PPO.

concepts.name: GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization)
concepts.definition: Popularized by DeepSeek; used for math and code. Generates multiple outputs per query and learns relative preferences within the group.

concepts.name: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
concepts.definition: Alternative to PPO; directly optimizes the model on preference pairs without a separate reward model.

concepts.name: PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization)
concepts.definition: Classic RLHF algorithm; uses a reward model + policy gradient. Older but still used.

concepts.name: Tool Calling / Function Calls
concepts.definition: LLMs cannot actually make function calls — they only output tokens. Through fine-tuning, they're trained to output a special token template like 'time = [calendar] [get_current_time] [result]' that the server-side parses and executes. The result is fed back into the next prompt.
concepts.key_insight: Models output TOKENS that the server interprets. The actual call is server-side.

concepts.name: Tool Call Template
concepts.definition: A textual convention the model is trained to produce: <tool_name> <parameter> <placeholder for result>. After data is filled in, the model sees the result and continues.

concepts.name: Model Serving
concepts.definition: After post-training, weights are frozen and deployed to GPUs. Users send queries and receive responses. Internal weights are not changed at inference time.

concepts.name: GPU Orchestration (Pipeline Parallelism)
concepts.definition: When a model is too large to fit on one GPU, different layers sit on different GPUs. An orchestrator passes data between them. Output flows back to the orchestrator → next GPU → eventually final prediction.

concepts.name: Vocabulary Size
concepts.definition: Number of tokens the model knows. Output probability distribution has one probability per vocabulary token. The transformer ends with a linear layer that maps N × D → N × vocabulary.

concepts.name: Context Window (recap)
concepts.definition: Max tokens the model can attend to. 1M context ≠ 1M tokens of info — every token gets context from all 1M others (1M × 1M propagation). KV cache is critical.

concepts.name: KV Cache (recap)
concepts.definition: Memoization of K and V vectors for previously-seen tokens. Prevents re-computing the entire N × N similarity matrix on every new token.

concepts.name: Transformer Input/Output Dimensions
concepts.definition: Input: N tokens → N × D embeddings (D = 8192, etc.). After position encoding: N × D. After norm: N × D. After QKV: three N × D. After attention: N × D. After feed-forward: N × D (with intermediate N × 4D → N × D). After final linear: N × vocabulary.

concepts.name: Data Shortage
concepts.definition: We are running out of publicly available training data. Synthetic data and more social-media / robot data are options, but each has tradeoffs.

qa_themes.answer: The output is human-written once, but losses are computed automatically. The model is not penalized by a human.

qa_themes.theme: How do you penalize on tokens with little context?
qa_themes.answer: Deferred. The model still gets a loss signal at every position; the question is meaningful for further class discussion.

qa_themes.theme: What is the input/output size of the transformer?
qa_themes.answer: N tokens → N × D throughout attention and feed-forward. The final linear layer maps N × D → N × vocabulary. Output shape = N × |V|.

qa_themes.theme: How does tool calling actually work?
qa_themes.answer: The model outputs a special token template; the server interprets it and executes the function; the result is appended to the prompt and the model continues.

qa_themes.theme: What are some modern preference optimization algorithms?
qa_themes.answer: GRPO (DeepSeek, math/code), DPO (direct preference), PPO (classic RLHF). Sigmoid is the conceptual anchor.

qa_themes.theme: Why does input token count usually exceed output token count?
qa_themes.answer: Apps pass documents, search results, page contents as input. Output is the model's summarized response.

key_takeaways: Pre-training: tokenize massive data, predict next token at every position, cross-entropy loss
SFT: human-written QA pairs for format/tone/jargon
Tool calling is a TEXTUAL convention — the model emits tokens; the server interprets
Preference optimization refines behavior with reward signals (GRPO, DPO, PPO)
Model serving freezes weights; KV cache and vocabulary are key knobs for cost/performance
